summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.

Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Anagarika Munindra (~1963–1967) and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1965–1967), and later taught Sharon Salzberg, Joseph Goldstein, Jack Kornfield, and Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua (b. 1938) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Assistant Lecturer in Pali (~1964) and Dean (1987) at the University of Calcutta, and held the head post at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was a lecturer at Sanskrit College and University (attested 1966) and served at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Dipankar Bhattacharya works in Indology and linguistics. He pursued a PhD at National Sanskrit University (2023–2026) and was appointed Project Manager (Content & Research) at Rishihood University in 2025.

Dipesh Chakrabarty (b. 1948) works in history, archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1983–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago (1995).

Dirk H. A. Kolff (b. 1938) is an Indologist and historian. He completed his MA and doctorate at Leiden University, where he served as a lecturer (1967) and held the Chair of Indian History (1971–2003).
Dirk Huizinga (1840–1903) studied at the University of Groningen from ~1858 to 1867. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Groningen from 1870 to 1901.

Dirk Jan Hoens (1920–2003) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed a PhD (1939–1951) under Jan Gonda and a Dr.Theol. (-1955) at Utrecht University, where he also served as an assistant from 1948 to 1982.

Dirk Schmidt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied for a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2026), where he also served as a PhD student and teaching assistant in 2022.

Dirk van Hinloopen Labberton (1874–1961) was a linguist and Indologist with doctorates from Leiden and Amsterdam. He taught at Gymnasium Willem III, Bestuursschool, and the University of Tokyo, and founded and led the Theosofisch Lyceum (~1933–1937).

Divya Prakash Pathak works in computational linguistics and Indology. After earning an MA in Sanskrit from Jawaharlal Nehru University (2021–2023), he became a Research Scholar at the University of Delhi in 2023.

Divyaraj Amiya specializes in Indology and linguistics. As of 2026, he is attested as a faculty member at the University of Tübingen and a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich.

Diwakar Acharya (b. 1969) is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned an MA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and a PhD at Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler. He taught at Kyoto University (2006–2016) before joining Oxford in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu. He served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from ~1912 to 1932.

Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij (1853–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Minaev, Jagić, Potebnja, and Bergaigne. He held professorships at Odesa University (1882–1887), Kazan (1887–1888), Kharkiv (1888–1905), and Saint Petersburg State University (from 1905).

Dmitry Aleksandrovich Suleykin (1900–1948) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He worked as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from 1935 to 1938.

Dmitry Danilov is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Mariupol State University, the University of Vienna, and Vasyl' Stus Donetsk National University, and was a PhD candidate at the H.S. Skovoroda Institute of Philosophy in 2015.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Minaev in St. Petersburg and Berthold Delbrück at Jena. He held posts at Saint Petersburg, the University of Tartu (from 1898), and Voronezh State University (~1918–1920).
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
